title: Yeast Selection for Non-Alcoholic Beer Production
content: The production of non-alcoholic beer has become a significant area of interest in the brewing industry, driven by increasing consumer demand for healthier beverages and the global trend toward reduced alcohol consumption. One of the key technological challenges is controlling ethanol formation during fermentation while maintaining the final product’s acceptable sensory characteristics. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the effect of yeast incubation with wort at low temperatures on the fermentation process and quality parameters of non-alcoholic beer. Experimental studies were carried out at the Educational and Scientific Centre for Fermentation Product Production of Almaty Technological University using a NANO BREWERY TYPE 50 L system. Three yeast strains were evaluated: Saccharomycodes ludwigii U-2012, Pichia kluveri U-3623, and Torulaspora delbrueckii U-1538. The influence of low fermentation temperatures on yeast cell growth, ethanol accumulation, and beer organoleptic characteristics was investigated. The results showed that decreasing the fermentation temperature significantly affected yeast metabolic activity and ethanol production. Among the studied S. ludwigii U-2012 strains, the cultivar demonstrated the lowest enzymatic activity and produced non-alcoholic beer with favorable organoleptic properties, providing an ethanol concentration of 0.45–0.47% vol/L when using wort with an extract volume of 6.62%. The optimal fermentation temperature for producing beer with improved quality characteristics was determined to be 6–8 °C.
